banh-ong-khmer-soc-trang.name: Soc Trang Khmer Bánh Ống Pandan Rice Cakes
banh-ong-khmer-soc-trang.serving_basis: About eight small tube cakes for four, served warm or at room temperature.
banh-ong-khmer-soc-trang.description: Soc Trang Khmer bánh ống is made from soaked rice ground with pandan water and steamed in tube molds. Bếp Việt adapts the locally documented method for a home batch, served with grated coconut, toasted sesame and sugar.
banh-ong-khmer-soc-trang.finished_dish: Soft, airy steamed cakes fragrant with pandan and rice, served with grated coconut, toasted sesame and a little sugar.
banh-ong-khmer-soc-trang.serving: Remove the cakes from their molds while warm and top with grated coconut, toasted sesame and sugar. Eat the same day for the softest texture.
tips: Soak the rice fully and drain it well before grinding; the mixture should be moist and fluffy, not runny.
Fill the molds only about two-thirds full so steam can circulate and the cakes can expand.
Preheat the molds and steam in small batches; handle the hot molds and steam carefully.
banh-ong-khmer-soc-trang.image_alt: Soc Trang Khmer bánh ống pandan rice cakes topped with grated coconut and toasted sesame on a complete plate; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
banh-ong-khmer-soc-trang.time_note: About 5 hours 5 minutes, including 4 hours to soak the rice.

ingredients.name: Fragrant rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse and soak separately; choose fresh, aromatic rice.

ingredients.name: Local plain rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse and soak with the fragrant rice; long-grain plain rice can be used.

ingredients.name: Pandan leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse, blend with water and strain to make pandan water.

ingredients.name: Pandan water
ingredients.notes: Blend pandan leaves with water and strain; use enough to grind the rice.

ingredients.name: Grated coconut
ingredients.notes: Freshly grated coconut, for serving.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle over the cakes or mix lightly with coconut to taste.

ingredients.name: White sesame seeds
ingredients.notes: Toast until fragrant and cool.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: A small pinch brings out the rice flavor.

preparation_steps: Rinse the two kinds of rice separately and soak in clean water for about 4 hours. Drain for 20–30 minutes, then grind with pandan water into a moist, fine batter. Sieve out any coarse grains.
Toast the sesame in a dry pan until fragrant. Prepare clean bánh ống molds and a steamer; bring the water to a boil and warm the molds in the steamer.
cooking_steps: Stir the salt into the rice batter. Spoon batter into the hot tube molds without packing it down, filling each about two-thirds full.
Cover and steam each batch for about 2–3 minutes, until the cake sets and is cooked through. Remove carefully with a suitable tool and repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve the cakes warm with grated coconut, toasted sesame and sugar. Adjust the sugar on each portion.

bun-goi-da-soc-trang.name: Soc Trang Bún Gỏi Dà Noodle Soup
aliases: Soc Trang rice noodles with spring-roll-style toppings
bun-goi-da-soc-trang.serving_basis: Four bowls of noodles with pork, shrimp, vegetables and gently sour broth, served with broth poured over or alongside.
bun-goi-da-soc-trang.description: Bún gỏi dà is a signature Soc Trang noodle dish that evokes the way gỏi cuốn is eaten, with rice noodles, shrimp, pork, fresh greens, peanuts and tamarind broth. Bếp Việt adapts a small-pot method with fermented soybean paste and pork-bone broth, serving the broth separately so the greens stay crisp.
bun-goi-da-soc-trang.finished_dish: A bowl of noodles with pink shrimp, tender pork, fresh greens, roasted peanuts and gently sweet-sour broth fragrant with fermented soybean paste.
bun-goi-da-soc-trang.serving: Arrange noodles and greens in bowls, add pork, shrimp and peanuts. Pour on hot broth to taste or serve it alongside; offer lime and chili separately.
tips: Skim the broth while simmering the bones for a clearer, cleaner flavor.
Add tamarind and fermented soybean paste gradually; the sweet-sour flavor should be gentle and should not overpower the shrimp and pork.
Briefly blanch fresh rice noodles if needed, drain them and pour on the broth just before serving.
dish_type: Noodles with broth and fresh greens
search_terms: how to cook bún gỏi dà
bun-goi-da-soc-trang.image_alt: A bowl of Soc Trang bún gỏi dà with rice noodles, shrimp, pork, fresh greens, peanuts and tamarind broth on a complete serving plate; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
bun-goi-da-soc-trang.time_note: About 1 hour 50 minutes, including broth simmering.

ingredients.name: Fresh rice vermicelli
ingredients.notes: Briefly blanch in boiling water if needed, then drain.

ingredients.name: Small river shrimp or small tiger shrimp
ingredients.notes: Rinse and devein; leave the shells on for cooking if you like.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Rinse, simmer until cooked, cool slightly and slice thinly.

ingredients.name: Pork bones
ingredients.notes: Blanch briefly and rinse before making the broth.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For simmering the bones; add hot water if needed.

ingredients.name: Ripe tamarind
ingredients.notes: Soak in hot water, mash and strain the juice.

ingredients.name: Fermented soybeans
ingredients.notes: Lightly crush or coarsely blend.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Season gradually for a gentle sweet-sour balance.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add at the end, accounting for the saltiness of the fermented soybeans.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and crush.

ingredients.name: Lettuce
ingredients.notes: Rinse well, drain and tear into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: Use Thai basil, mint or herbs commonly served with noodles; rinse well.

ingredients.name: Bean sprouts
ingredients.notes: Rinse and drain.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Lightly crush.

ingredients.name: Fried shallots
ingredients.notes: Optional topping.

ingredients.name: Lime and chili
ingredients.notes: Serve separately so each person can adjust the seasoning.

preparation_steps: Blanch the pork bones in boiling water for 2 minutes, discard the water and rinse. Rinse the shrimp and pork; wash and drain the greens, bean sprouts and herbs.
Soak the tamarind in about 100 ml hot water and strain out the seeds. Crush the fermented soybeans and garlic; roast and crush the peanuts if needed.
cooking_steps: Put the bones and 1.8 liters of water in a pot. Bring to a boil and skim the foam, then lower the heat and simmer gently for about 50 minutes.
Add the pork belly to the broth and simmer for about 20 minutes until cooked. Remove, cool slightly and slice. Add the shrimp and cook for 3–5 minutes until just done; remove and peel.
Strain the broth if needed. Stir in the tamarind juice, fermented soybeans, sugar and fish sauce; simmer gently for 5 minutes and balance the sweet, sour and savory flavors.
Divide the noodles, greens, bean sprouts, pork and shrimp among four bowls. Top with peanuts and fried shallots. Pour on hot broth or serve it alongside, with lime and chili.

hu-tieu-ca-ri-vinh-chau.name: Vĩnh Châu Duck Curry Rice Noodles
hu-tieu-ca-ri-vinh-chau.serving_basis: Four bowls of rice noodles with duck curry in coconut milk and fresh accompaniments.
hu-tieu-ca-ri-vinh-chau.description: Vĩnh Châu curry noodles combine rice noodles with duck cooked in curry, lemongrass and coconut milk. Bếp Việt adapts the local specialty documented by Soc Trang travel sources for a home pot, using Muscovy duck, taro and a moderate amount of curry seasoning.
hu-tieu-ca-ri-vinh-chau.finished_dish: Tender duck and soft taro in golden curry fragrant with lemongrass and coconut milk; chewy rice noodles are served with bean sprouts and herbs.
hu-tieu-ca-ri-vinh-chau.serving: Divide the noodles, duck and taro among bowls and ladle over the hot curry. Serve bean sprouts, herbs and lime separately.
tips: Choose fresh Muscovy duck; clean it thoroughly and drain before marinating.
Marinate the duck for at least 30 minutes to infuse it with lemongrass and curry, then brown it before adding liquid.
Simmer gently so the meat softens without boiling the coconut milk over; add hot water if the curry becomes too thick.
hu-tieu-ca-ri-vinh-chau.image_alt: A bowl of Vĩnh Châu curry noodles with rice noodles, Muscovy duck, taro and coconut curry broth, herbs alongside; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
hu-tieu-ca-ri-vinh-chau.time_note: About 2 hours 20 minutes, including 30 minutes to marinate the duck.

ingredients.name: Muscovy duck
ingredients.notes: Cut into serving pieces, clean and drain.

ingredients.name: Dried rice noodles
ingredients.notes: Soak and cook according to package directions, then drain.

ingredients.name: Coconut milk
ingredients.notes: Use full-fat coconut milk and stir before measuring.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For simmering the duck until tender.

ingredients.name: Taro
ingredients.notes: Peel and cube; part of it may be replaced with sweet potato.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Mince some and bruise the remainder.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Curry powder
ingredients.notes: Choose a mildly hot blend and adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Use part for the marinade and adjust the rest at the end.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balance the flavor without making it noticeably sweet.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the aromatics and duck.

ingredients.name: Bean sprouts
ingredients.notes: Rinse and drain.

ingredients.name: Thai basil
ingredients.notes: Rinse, drain and serve alongside.

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.notes: Cut into wedges and serve separately.

preparation_steps: Rinse and cut the duck into serving pieces; drain well. Marinate for 30 minutes with half the curry powder, some fish sauce, sugar and minced lemongrass.
Peel and cube the taro; briefly soak and drain. Mince the shallots, garlic and lemongrass; rinse the bean sprouts and Thai basil. Soak the dried noodles as directed.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the shallots, garlic and lemongrass until fragrant. Add the remaining curry powder and stir for about 20 seconds, taking care not to burn it.
Add the marinated duck and brown the surfaces. Pour in the water, bring to a boil and skim; partially cover, reduce the heat and simmer for 40–45 minutes until nearly tender.
Add the taro and simmer for about 15 minutes until soft. Stir in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 8–10 minutes; season with the remaining fish sauce.
Cook the noodles until just tender and divide among bowls. Add duck and taro, ladle over the hot curry, and serve with bean sprouts, Thai basil and lime.

xoi-xiem-chau-doc.name: Châu Đốc Xôi Xiêm Coconut Sticky Rice
xoi-xiem-chau-doc.serving_basis: Four portions of coconut sticky rice served with palm-sugar egg sauce.
xoi-xiem-chau-doc.description: Xôi Xiêm is a sweet snack associated with Châu Đốc, made with glutinous rice, coconut milk and, in some versions, pandan and durian. Bếp Việt adapts a home version served with an egg, palm-sugar and coconut sauce, cooked separately for easier control of its thickness.
xoi-xiem-chau-doc.finished_dish: Glossy, tender sticky rice fragrant with coconut milk and pandan, served with lightly thickened palm-sugar egg sauce and optional durian.
xoi-xiem-chau-doc.serving: Spoon the warm sticky rice onto plates, add sauce to taste and top with fresh durian if using. Serve promptly.
tips: Soak the glutinous rice for at least 3 hours and drain it so the grains steam evenly.
Stir the egg sauce continuously over low heat; do not let it boil hard or the egg may curdle.
Durian has a strong flavor; use a modest amount or omit it for a lighter coconut flavor.
xoi-xiem-chau-doc.image_alt: A plate of Châu Đốc xôi Xiêm with coconut sticky rice, amber egg sauce, pandan and durian alongside; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
xoi-xiem-chau-doc.time_note: About 4 hours, including 3 hours to soak the rice.

ingredients.name: Glutinous rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse, soak for 3 hours and drain.

ingredients.name: Coconut milk
ingredients.notes: Use some to flavor the rice and the remainder for the sauce.

ingredients.name: Pandan leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse and tie into a bundle for steaming with the rice.

ingredients.name: Palm sugar
ingredients.notes: Shave or chop finely so it melts easily.

ingredients.name: Egg
ingredients.notes: Lightly beat before cooking the sauce.

ingredients.name: Durian
ingredients.notes: Separate the flesh and remove the seeds; optional.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide a small pinch between the rice and sauce.

preparation_steps: Rinse the glutinous rice until the water is mostly clear, soak it in clean water for 3 hours and drain. Rinse and tie the pandan leaves; shave the palm sugar.
Shake the coconut milk well. Lightly beat the egg in a heatproof bowl and prepare a small saucepan and steamer.
cooking_steps: Mix the rice with about 120 ml coconut milk and a pinch of salt. Spread it in a clean-cloth-lined steamer, place the pandan on top and steam for 25–30 minutes until tender and translucent.
In a small saucepan, combine the remaining coconut milk, palm sugar and a pinch of salt. Warm over low heat until the sugar dissolves. Slowly whisk a few spoonfuls of the warm mixture into the egg.
Strain the egg mixture back into the saucepan and stir continuously over low heat for 5–7 minutes until it lightly coats a spoon. Do not let it boil hard.
Divide the sticky rice among plates, spoon over the warm sauce and add durian if using. Serve promptly.

com-dep-khmer-soc-trang.name: Soc Trang Khmer Cốm Dẹp Flattened Rice
aliases: Khmer cốm dẹp for Ok Om Bok
com-dep-khmer-soc-trang.serving_basis: Four portions of flattened rice mixed with coconut, served after resting to soften.
com-dep-khmer-soc-trang.description: Cốm dẹp is a Khmer delicacy associated with Soc Trang and the Ok Om Bok festival. Young rice is pounded flat, then mixed with grated coconut, sugar and coconut water. Bếp Việt adapts a small-batch method and briefly rests the mixture so the grains soften and absorb the flavors.
com-dep-khmer-soc-trang.finished_dish: Soft, chewy flattened rice fragrant with young rice and fresh coconut, gently sweet and creamy.
com-dep-khmer-soc-trang.serving: Serve the flattened rice after mixing and resting for about 15 minutes. It may be placed on clean banana leaves or eaten with a spoon.
tips: Use fresh, dry cốm dẹp from a reliable food source.
Add coconut water gradually; the grains should become soft and chewy without turning soggy.
Taste before adding all the sugar, since the rice and coconut vary in sweetness.
search_terms: how to make flattened rice with coconut
com-dep-khmer-soc-trang.image_alt: A complete plate of Soc Trang Khmer cốm dẹp mixed with grated coconut and sugar, with green banana leaf; original Bếp Việt image on transparency.
com-dep-khmer-soc-trang.time_note: About 25 minutes, including 15 minutes for the rice to soften.

ingredients.name: Cốm dẹp (flattened young rice)
ingredients.notes: Choose clean flattened young rice with no damp or musty odor.

ingredients.name: Grated coconut
ingredients.notes: Freshly grated coconut; reserve a little for the topping.

ingredients.name: Fresh coconut water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually; the amount used depends on how dry the rice is.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Use granulated sugar or finely shaved palm sugar and adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: A small pinch brings out the coconut flavor.

ingredients.name: Banana leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse and dry; use to line the plate or wrap portions.

preparation_steps: Pick out any debris from the flattened rice. Grate the coconut and reserve a little for garnish; strain the coconut water if it contains sediment.
Wipe the banana leaves clean and cut them to line a plate or wrap individual portions. Measure the sugar and salt.
cooking_steps: Put the flattened rice in a wide bowl and mix with the grated coconut, sugar and a pinch of salt.
Drizzle in the coconut water a little at a time, gently turning the mixture so the grains absorb it evenly. Stop when the grains are soft and chewy but still separate.
Cover and rest for about 15 minutes. Taste and adjust the sugar if needed, top with the reserved coconut and serve.
